functions.author: E. Harlow
functions.title: Surveyor's Log
pages:
Day 1.
Crown survey, southern
wetlands. The map shows
open marsh here. The map
is wrong. The trees are
black to the core and they
weep. No birdsong at all.

Day 3.
The roots are not wood.
I cut one to check the
grain. It is bone. Old,
yellowed, hard as stone.
I did not cut another.

Day 6.
A figure at the edge of
the fog, between two
trunks. Tall. Thin. Too
still. I raised my glass
and it was simply gone.
Only black smoke, sinking.

Day 9.
It is there whenever I
am not looking. I have
started to feel it the way
you feel a draught.

It has been closer
each time.

Day 11.
Built this shack for
shelter. Left the chart
on the desk.

If you are reading this,
do not finish my survey.
The mire does not want
to be measured.

functions.author: Tobias Wren
functions.title: Tally
pages:
came for the
black timber.
best price in three
counties. nobody said
why.

IIII

IIII IIII

wind came through again
tonight. all at once,
like the whole forest
breathed in. leaves
everywhere. then nothing.

IIII IIII IIII

saw it by the water.
two white lights where
a face should be.
it did not blink.
neither did I.

IIII IIII IIII II

it only moves when you
look away. so I stopped
looking away.

I have not slept.

it was gone in a puff
of black mist when I
walked at it. the ground
where it stood was cold
as a cellar.

I am going home
tomorrow.

functions.author: Unknown
functions.title: Field Notes
pages:
Flora of the mire:

- black weeping tree.
  no sap. the wood is
  cold even at noon.
- pale grass. dry as
  paper. crumbles.
- small white stalks
  shaped like crosses.

Fauna:

none.

No deer, no frogs, no
insects. Even the
crows turn back at
the tree line.

Water: dark. Still.
Does not reflect the
sky properly. Shows the
trees, but not me.

I checked twice.

Note to self:
the roots grip the
ground like hands. They
were not like this
yesterday. They were
further from the hut.

functions.author: J.
functions.title: To Mara
pages:
Mara,

I found the cabin you
wrote about. The door
was gone. Your boots
were by the stove.
Your journal was not.

I keep finding pages.
Nailed nowhere, just
lying in the moss like
someone dropped them
for me to find.

They are in your hand.

Every page I pick up,
the wind dies down.
Every time, the same.
Like the whole wood is
holding its breath to
hear me read.

I saw you tonight. At
the edge of the water.
You were too tall.
You had no face.

I am sorry, Mara.
I am coming to find you.

functions.author: Whoever is left
functions.title: Rules
pages:
RULES OF THE MIRE

1. Do not stare at it.
   It notices.
2. Do not walk toward
   it. It will not be
   there, and then it
   will be behind you.

3. When the wind stops,
   stop with it.
4. Count the trees each
   morning. If there is
   one more, leave.
5. Never take the pages.
   Read them, put them
   back.

6. It cannot hurt you.
   That is not the same
   as being safe.

7. If you find all of
   the pages, it will
   come to find you.
